FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Textile Machinery and Accessories Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textiles Division 
Council. 


Crank shaft of cotton looms transmits the power from motor to machinery and controls the complete operation. 
Service life of the cotton loom is determined by performance of crank shaft. 


This standard was originally published in 1963 and subsequently revised in 1979. This revision has been made in 
the light of experience gained since its publication and to incorporate the following major changes: 


a) Title of the standard has been modified; 

b) Marking and packing clauses have been modified; 
c) Sampling clause has been incorporated; and 

d) References to Indian Standards have been updated. 


The composition of the committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is listed in Annex D. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 2531 : 2023 


Indian Standard 


TEXTILES — CRANK SHAFT FOR COTTON LOOMS — 
SPECIFICATION 


( Second Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements of crank 
shafts used in non-automatic and automatic looms. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which, through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision, and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent editions of the standards listed in Annex A. 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


3.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following 
definitions shall apply. 


3.1 Left-Hand Loom — A loom with the starting 
handle on its left hand side. 


3.2 Right-Hand Loom — A loom with the starting 
handle on its right hand side. 


NOTE — If an observer stands near the delivery end of the 
loom and looks against the run of the warp, the side on his 
left hand is the left-hand side of the loom and the side on his 
right hand is the right-hand side of the loom. 


CRANK SHAFT 
JOURNAL 


CRANK PIN 


3.3 Reed Space (of the Loom) — Maximum space 
available on the loom for the insertion of a reed, that 
is, the overall width of the reed which can be fixed 
on the loom. 


3.4 Crank Radius — The perpendicular distance 
between the axis of crank shaft journal and the axis 
of its crank pin. 


4 MANUFACTURE 
4.1 Material 


Crank shalt shall be manufactured from bars 
conforming to Class 2A of IS 1875. 


4.2 Workmanship and Finish 


The shaft shall be straight and free from rust. Crank 
pin and the journals of the crank shaft shall be 
smooth finished and polished. The roughness value 
(Ra) of crank pins and the journals shall be within 
1.6 um to 6.3 um. 


4.3 Shape 
The crank shaft shall be as shown in Fig. 1. 


NOTE — Crank shafts of the, looms having reed space of 
1 500 mm and above should have two supports between the 
cranks. 


CRANK PIN 


Fic. 1 TYPICAL CRANK SHAFT 


IS 2531 : 2023 


5 REQUIREMENTS 
5.1 Dimensions 


The dimensions of the crank shaft shall be as per the 
manufacturers standard design. The diameter of 
crank shaft shall have a fit of h8 according to 
IS 919 (Part 1). The length of crank shaft shall be 
within coarse class deviations for linear dimensions 
specified in IS 2102 (Partl) and reproduced in 
Annex B for ready reference. 


5.2 True Running 


The journals and the crank pins of the crank shaft 
shall run true. However, when tested by the method 
given in C-l, out-of-true running, of the journals and 
the crank pins if present, shall not exceed 0.025 mm 
and 0.013 mm respectively. 


5.3 Parallelism 


Each of the crank pins shall be parallel to both the 
journals. However, when tested by the method given 
in C-2, a deviation of 0.05 mm from parallelism 
shall be permitted. 


5.4 Crank Radius 

The variation in the crank radius of the crank shaft 
when tested by the method given in C-3 shall not 
exceed 0.2 mm. 

5.5 Screw Threads 

The journal of the crank shaft on the cog wheel side 
shall preferably be provided at its end over a length 
of 45 mm with screw threads conforming to IS 4218 
(Part 4). 

6 MARKING 


6.1 Each crank shaft shall be marked, at a suitable 


SURFACE PLATE 


place, with the following information: 


a) Manufacturer’s name, initials and trade- 
mark, if any; 

b) Reed space of the loom on which it is to be 
used; 


c) Number of crank shafts in the case; 

а) ‘R’ or ‘L’ depending upon the right-hand or 
left-hand loom on which it is to be used; 

e) Gross and net mass; 

f) Lot/batch number; 

g) Country of origin; and 


h) Any other information required by the law 
in force and/or by the buyer. 


6.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, апа the 
products may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


7 PACKING 


The crank shaft shall be coated lightly with rust 
preventive grease and shall be held in semicircular 
slots cut out in four parallel wooden planks fixed in 
vertical position inside a wooden case. The slots 
should be suitable protected so that wood does not 
come in direct contact with the shaft. The wooden 
case shall be strong enough to withstand the hazards 
of transit. 


8 SAMPLING 
Unless otherwise agreed to between the buyer and 
the seller, to ascertain the conformity of crank shaft 


to the requirements of this specification, or as 
specified in IS 2500 (Part 1) shall be followed.

ANNEX C 
(Clauses 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4) 


METHODS OF TESTS 


C-1 TRUE RUNNING OF JOURNALS AND 
CRANK PINS 


C-1.1 А surface plate, two V-blocks and a 
micrometer dial gauge shall be used for the purpose 
of this test. 


C-1.2 True Running of Journals 


Set the V-blocks on the surface plate. Take a crank 
shaft and mount it with its journals in the V- blocks 
(see Fig. 2). Set the micrometer dial gauge in such a 
way that its anvil head is held in contact with the 
surface of one of the journals of the crank shaft. 
Adjust the pointer of the dial gauge to zero position. 
Rotate the shaft once. Observe the maximum 
deflection of the needle of the micrometer dial gauge 
on both sides of the zero position. Add the two 
values and divide the sum by two. Repeat the test at 
4 more places along the length of the same journal 
and at 5 places along the length of the second 
journal. 


C-1.3 True Running of Crank Pins 


Set the V-blocks on the surface plate. Take a crank 
shaft and mount it with its pins in the V-blocks (see 
Fig. 3). Set the micrometer dial gauge in such a way 
that its anvil head is held in contact with the surface 
of one of the crank pins (see Note). Adjust the 
pointer of the dial gauge to zero position. Rotate the 
shaft once. Observe the maximum deflection of the 
pointer of the micrometer dial gauge on both sides 
of the zero position. Add the two values and divide 
the sum by two. Repeat the test at one more place 
along the length of the same pin and at two places 
on the second crank pin. 


NOTE — The point of contact should be selected at about 
10 mm from either end of the crank pin. 


C-1.4 Report the crank shaft to be in conformity 
with the requirements of 5.2 if none of the values as 
obtained in С-1.2 апа C-1.3 exceeds 0.025 mm and 
0.013 mm respectively. 


C-2. PARALLELISM OF CRANK SHAFT 
JOURNALS AND CRANK PINS 


C-2.1 A surface plate, two V-blocks and a dial 
indicator shall he used for the purpose of this test. 


C-2.2 Set the V-blocks on the surface plate. Take a 
crank shaft and mount it with its journals in the 
V-blocks so that the crank pins are in their lowest 
position (see Fig. 4). 


C-2.3 Mark two points A and B, 50 mm apart at the 
highest surface of one of the journals of the crank 


shaft. Set the indicator at point A and adjust its 
pointer at zero position. Move the indicator from A 
to B (see Note). Record the maximum indicator 
reading with its proper algebraic sign (that is, plus 
or minus). Mark two points C and D, 50 mm apart at 
the highest surface of the crank pin which is nearest 
to the journal tested as above. Set the indicator at 
point C and adjust its pointer at zero position. Move 
the indicator from C to D. Record the maximum 
indicator reading with its proper algebraic sign (that 
is, plus or minus). Determine the algebraic 
difference between the two values measured on the 
journal and on the crank pin. 


NOTE — The indicator may be moved from A to B by 
moving its base along the edge of a parallel which has been 
set parallel to the sides of V-blocks. 


C-2.4 Rotate the shaft through 90° (a quarter 
rotation) and keep it in this position by suitable 
means. Repeat the procedure prescribed in C-2.3. 


C-2.5 Repeat the procedure prescribed in C-2.3 and 
C-2.4 on the second journal and second crank pin. 


C-2.6 Report the crank shaft to be in conformity 
with the requirements of 5.3 if none of the values 
observed in C-2.3, С-2.4 and C-2.5 exceeds 
0.05 mm. 


C-3 CRANK RADIUS 


C-3.1 Surface plate, two V-blocks and a vernier 
height gauge shall be used for the purpose of this 
test. 


C-3.2 Set the V-blocks on the surface plate. Take a 
crank shaft and mount it with its journals in the 
V-blocks in such a way that the crank pins are in the 
lowest position (see Fig. 5). Measure the height of 
the top of the crank pin in this position at a point A 
with the vernier height gauge. 


C-3.3 Rotate the crank shaft through 180° so that the 
crank pins are in their highest position (as shown in 
the dotted lines in Fig. 5). Keep the crank pins in this 
position by suitable means (see Note 1). ‘Measure 
with the vernier height gauge the height of the top of 
the crank pin in this position at a point B 
corresponding to the point A (see Note 2). 


NOTES 


1 The crank pins can be kept in this position by holding the 
crank shaft against an angle plate. 


2 The point B corresponding to the point A may 
automatically be obtained by keeping the height gauge in 
the same position and raising the scriber to the required 
height. 


IS 2531 : 2023 


C-3.4 Subtract the height obtained as in C-3.2 from 
the height obtained as in C-3.3. Divide the value so 
obtained by two (This value shall be equal to the 
radius of the crank). 


C-3.5 Repeat the test on the second crank pin. 


C-3.6 Report the crank shaft to be in conformity 
with the requirements of 5.4 if the difference in the 
values obtained in C-3.4 and C-3.5 is not more than 
0.2 mm. 


IS 2531 : 2023

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
